author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both the page and the machine-readable route
summary: A specialty on the request narrows both the /vets.html page and the /vets machine-readable route to the veterinarians holding that specialty. Match is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive, never a prefix. Blank or spaces-only is treated as absent; an unknown specialty yields an empty list with a success status; no parameter behaves as today. URL contract only, no visible control.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty that some veterinarians hold, when the veterinarian page is requested with that specialty, only those veterinarians are shown, a page at a time.
Given a specialty that some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable directory is requested with that specialty, only those veterinarians are returned.
Given a specialty supplied in a different letter case than the stored name, when either surface is requested with it, it matches.
Given a value that is part of a specialty name but not the whole name, when either surface is requested with it, no veterinarian matches.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is requested with it, the result is an empty veterinarian list with a success status (HTTP 200).
Given a specialty that is blank or only spaces, when either surface is requested, the result is the same as the surface requested without the parameter.
Given no specialty on the request, when either surface is requested, it behaves as it does today.
Given a filtered veterinarian page whose matches span more than one page, when a paging link is followed, the link carries the specialty and the next filtered page is shown.
Given the machine-readable directory (REQ-VET-003), when it is requested without a specialty, it returns each veterinarian and their specialties with a success status, unchanged from today.
non_goals: A visible filter control (form or dropdown) on the veterinarian page is out of this slice; the filter is a URL contract only and a control may follow.
Free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope per the narrowed NG-9; only whole-name specialty filtering is in.
Pet and visit search remain out of scope.
notes: REQ-VET-003 designates the /vets machine-readable route a supported surface (reinstated with a fresh ID; withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and is not reused); this slice adds its first requested capability, the specialty filter. Empty/whitespace handling mirrors the empty owner search (REQ-OWN-002), including trimming surrounding spaces around a real value (PRD Veterinarian directory edge case 3). Open, non-blocking: no visible control this round; repeated specialty parameter binding is left to framework default. Whole-name case-insensitive match, NOT prefix — deliberately different from owner prefix search.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the existing vet feature package (system-design §Contracts, VetController row) with an optional whole-name, case-insensitive specialty filter on both /vets.html and /vets. Fresh ground: the filter is applied in VetController over the cached VetRepository.findAll() collection (equalsIgnoreCase in Java), NOT via a new Spring Data query — recorded in adr/2026-08-24-specialty-filter-in-controller.md. This deliberately diverges from the DB-level owner-search match so the filter stays uniform across H2/MySQL/PostgreSQL and avoids the vendor case-folding divergence already logged as a Known Defect for owner search. Empty/blank/spaces-only handling mirrors OwnerController.processFindForm normalization (null/blank + strip -> no filter). Oracle N/A (no IntelliJ MCP tools on this run); resolution of VetController/VetRepository/Vets/Vet verified by Read.
integration_points: VetController.showVetList('/vets.html') gains @RequestParam(required=false) String specialty; normalize (null/blank/strip -> absent), and when present filter the cached collection, paginate the FILTERED list in memory (PageImpl over a sublist), and add the effective specialty to the model so pagination links reproduce it.

VetController.showResourcesVetList('/vets') gains the same specialty param; filter the cached collection and wrap the result in the existing Vets element. Empty match -> Vets with empty vetList, HTTP 200 (no error path). No-param behavior unchanged.

vetList.html pagination links must carry the specialty: switch the string-built hrefs (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}) to the URL-builder form @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} so a null/absent specialty is omitted and a present one is URL-encoded.
Vets wrapper needs NO change — it already wraps List<Vet>; populate it with the filtered list.
VetRepository needs NO change under the recommended controller-side approach, even though the PRD file_targets lists it — file_targets is a product hint, not a mandate.

patterns.description: Empty-search normalization to mirror: null -> broadest, else strip(); blank/spaces-only collapses to no filter. Reuse this exact shape for the specialty param (PRD edge case 3: trim surrounding spaces around a real value).

Vet.getSpecialties() already returns specialties sorted by name; the filter predicate matches any specialty whose name equalsIgnoreCase the trimmed value. Specialties are FetchType.EAGER and the collection is cached, so no N+1 beyond today.

risks.risk: In-memory pagination over the filtered list must preserve 'no-param behaves as today' for /vets.html: same page size (5) and same vet ordering as the current findAll(pageable) path.
risks.mitigation: Either keep the existing findAll(pageable) path for the unfiltered case and add an in-memory-paged branch only when a filter is present, or, if unifying on one in-memory-paged path, apply a stable deterministic sort so unfiltered pages match today. Assert totalPages/totalItems/page content for the unfiltered case in tests.

risks.risk: Pushing the filter into a Spring Data query (e.g. findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) would reintroduce vendor-divergent case-folding (the PostgreSQL owner-search defect class), bypass the shared cache, and hit the @ManyToMany collection-fetch + pagination pitfall.
risks.mitigation: Filter in the controller over the cached findAll() collection with equalsIgnoreCase, per the ADR. Do not add a repository query.

risks.risk: A repeated specialty query parameter is unspecified (PRD Open Question).
risks.mitigation: Non-blocking: rely on the framework default single-value String binding (first value); no special handling this slice.

risks.risk: Whole-name vs prefix: the match must be whole-name equality, deliberately NOT the prefix rule used for owner search.
risks.mitigation: Use equalsIgnoreCase on the whole specialty name, not startsWith/contains; test showVetListHtmlWithSpecialtyPrefixShouldNotMatch is the guard.

notes: Verdict new (not covered/minor) because the Contracts Implements mapping had to gain REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004 and a genuine trade-off (in-memory controller filter vs. repository query) warranted recording so a future maintainer does not 'fix' it into a vendor-divergent DB query. Design-doc changes made: (1) new ADR adr/2026-08-24-specialty-filter-in-controller.md + index row in adr/README.md; (2) system-design.md Contracts VetController row updated (purpose + Implements REQ-VET-001/003/004, ADR back-link); (3) removed the now-stale Known Defects row 'machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' — REQ-VET-003 makes it a supported surface. Seeded specialties are radiology/surgery/dentistry (db/*/data.sql) — useful fixtures for the tests. No autofix records to audit. No new dependencies; no module/boundary change; dependency graph stays acyclic.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No injection sink: the specialty filter is an in-memory equalsIgnoreCase over the cached VetRepository.findAll() collection; no DB query or JPQL is built from the request parameter, so the equalsIgnoreCase/whole-name design avoids the owner-search vendor case-folding class and introduces no SQLi surface.

No reflected XSS: the request-derived specialty reaches the template only as the 'specialty' model attribute inside Thymeleaf @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} URL-builder expressions on the pagination hrefs; the link-expression query parameter is URL-encoded and the th:href attribute output is HTML-escaped, and the value is never rendered into HTML text or an unquoted/JS/CSS context. The vetList.html loop variable 'specialty' on line 20 iterates vet.specialties and is unrelated to the request parameter.

Error handling is fail-safe: normalizeSpecialty treats null/blank/whitespace-only as absent (no filter), an unmatched specialty yields an empty list with HTTP 200, and no exception text or internal detail is exposed on the filter path.

Data integrity: the path is read-only over a cached, seeded collection; PageImpl sublist paging is bounds-checked (start<size guard, Math.min end), no writes, no state mutation, no privilege boundary crossed.
In-memory filter+paging DoS surface is negligible: the veterinarian directory is a small seeded, cached collection, so the stream filter and subList carry no attacker-amplifiable cost.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Lambda variable `s` in the `anyMatch` predicate refers to a `Specialty` object. The single-character name is too terse when the outer parameter is already called `specialty` — a reader must deduce the type from the stream source. Rename to `sp` or `spec` to make the element type visible without a type lookup.
findings.fix: Replace `s -> s.getName()` with `sp -> sp.getName()` in the `filterBySpecialty` stream pipeline.

approved_aspects: normalizeSpecialty correctly mirrors OwnerController.processFindForm normalization (null/blank/strip → null) — verified by direct Read of OwnerController lines 98-104; oracle N/A (IntelliJ MCP not connected), claim grounded by Read
filterBySpecialty uses equalsIgnoreCase on the whole specialty name, not startsWith/contains, satisfying the whole-name match requirement

findPaginated routes null specialty to vetRepository.findAll(Pageable) (pre-existing cached paged path) and non-null specialty to vetRepository.findAll() (single cached collection entry) then PageImpl — consistent with the ADR
model.addAttribute("specialty", filter) with filter=null causes Thymeleaf URL builder to omit the parameter on unfiltered pages, which is the correct behaviour

Template pagination links all switched to @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} URL-builder form — cleaner than the prior preprocessed string literals and handles URL-encoding and null omission correctly; all five link positions updated consistently
Javadoc on normalizeSpecialty explains the cross-reference to the OwnerController pattern, giving a future reader the why without having to grep
ADR back-link comment in findPaginated steers a future maintainer away from replacing the in-memory filter with a repository query
Method lengths are all well under 30 lines; single-responsibility throughout

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: AC 3 ('given a specialty supplied in a different letter case, when either surface is requested, it matches') is only tested on the HTML surface. There is no test for the JSON/machine-readable surface asserting case-insensitive match (e.g. GET /vets?specialty=RADIOLOGY). The PRD acceptance criterion explicitly says 'either surface'.

AC 4 ('given a value that is part of a specialty name but not the whole name, when either surface is requested, no veterinarian matches') is only tested on the HTML surface via showVetListHtmlWithSpecialtyPrefixShouldNotMatch. There is no test asserting prefix-no-match on the JSON surface (GET /vets?specialty=rad). The PRD acceptance criterion explicitly says 'either surface'.

AC 6 ('given a specialty that is blank or only spaces, when either surface is requested, result is the same as without the parameter') is only tested on the HTML surface via showVetListHtmlWithBlankSpecialtyShouldReturnAllVets. There is no test asserting blank/whitespace-only behavior on the JSON surface (GET /vets?specialty=   ). The PRD acceptance criterion explicitly says 'either surface'.

PRD Veterinarian directory edge case 3 ('A specialty value carrying leading or trailing spaces around a real name matches the same as the name without them') has no test on either surface. No test exercises GET /vets.html?page=1&specialty=%20radiology%20 or GET /vets?specialty=%20radiology%20.

The showVetListHtmlFilteredPaginationLinksShouldCarrySpecialty test contains a for-loop ('for (int id = 10; id < 16; id++) { surgeons.add(surgeon(id)); }') in the test body. testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure states 'Tests are straight-line code: no if/else, switch, or loops in test bodies.' The loop should be replaced by calling surgeon() six times inline or by extracting a named list-building factory method.

The eight new test method names do not follow the BDD naming school mandated by testing-principles.md § Test Naming (applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward): 'the{Subject}Should{Outcome}'. Examples: 'showVetListHtmlFilteredBySpecialtyShowsOnlyMatchingVets' should be 'theVetListHtmlShouldShowOnlyVetsMatchingTheSpecialty'; 'showVetListHtmlWithSpecialtyPrefixShouldNotMatch' could be 'theVetListHtmlShouldNotMatchASpecialtyPrefix'. None of the eight new names begins with 'the' or follows the school.
findings.fix: Rename all eight new test methods to the 'the{Subject}Should{Outcome}' form. Pre-existing tests (showVetListHtml, showResourcesVetList) predate the school and are exempt per the brief — rename only the new ones added in this slice.

approved_aspects: All 10 tests pass on a clean build-pass run

Mocking usage stays within the 'tolerated' band: @MockitoBean on VetRepository is a pre-existing pattern in this @WebMvcTest class; the new tests extend it rather than introducing fresh mocking policy violations
surgeon(int id) fixture is a proper private factory method following the factory-method convention

AC 1 (HTML filter), AC 2 (JSON filter), AC 5 (unknown specialty + HTTP 200 on both surfaces), AC 7 (no-param behaves as today on both surfaces via pre-existing tests), and AC 8 (pagination carries specialty) all have direct, focused test coverage
showVetListHtmlFilteredBySpecialtyShowsOnlyMatchingVets verifies list size (1), confirming the filter excludes non-matching vets
showResourcesVetListFilteredBySpecialtyReturnsOnlyMatchingVets verifies both size and the specific matched vet id — strong identity assertion
Empty specialty assertions use model().attribute(..., hasSize(0)) — clearly communicates the empty-list expectation
Pagination test confirms both totalPages=2 and the presence of 'specialty=surgery' in the rendered HTML — both concerns tested
